name: Gavin Jones
life: “I still remember driving somebody who had just missed their job interview.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Gavin likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I was the next in line and angry. The customer gave me a ride to my interview when our time ran over.
appearance: Gavin is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a small enamel bird on the lapel, Gavin presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Gavin has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Gavin can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To get to the interview with the delayed customer.
family: Ellen Randall is Gavin’s second cousin. Gavin picks the meeting place. Ellen sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The late crossing*, Ellen says, “I can help if nobody smokes in the car. Asking made me feel more fragile than giving lifts.”
connections: Cora Yates. One customer gives up a place and another gets help arriving at an interview.

reactions.situation: A customer uses the free haircut to talk
reactions.response: Gavin lets the visitor say whether they would like a trim as well as a talk.

reactions.response: Gavin takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.
